name: How do duplexes compare with ADUs for income in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Should a homeowner build a duplex or add ADUs instead to maximize income on a Los Angeles lot?
mainEntity.text: Should a homeowner build a duplex or add ADUs instead to maximize income on a Los Angeles lot?

acceptedAnswer.text: Duplexes and ADUs solve different problems, even though both can improve income potential on a residential lot. A duplex is often better when the owner wants two full units, a clearer development story, and a stronger long-term rental product. ADUs can be attractive when the existing home stays in place, the project needs to be phased, or the lot is not ideal for full duplex construction. The better choice depends on whether the parcel can physically and legally support the desired density, plus how much capital is available up front. Duplexes usually involve more extensive permitting, design, and construction, but they can also deliver a more complete redevelopment of the site. ADUs may be faster or cheaper in some situations, but they may not unlock the same rent potential. Owners should compare expected rental income, total project cost, disruption to existing occupancy, and resale value. The right answer is often the option that best matches the lot, not the option with the highest unit count.
acceptedAnswer.description: A duplex usually creates more total living area and stronger rental income potential, while ADUs can be simpler to permit on some lots and less disruptive to the existing home. The better option depends on zoning, lot size, construction budget, and whether the owner wants one larger project or a phased strategy. The highest return is not always the biggest building.
